source.section: P3 lexical retrieval, evidence hydration and task context; exit gate G3
source.note: The plan names no clause identifiers. LEX-nn are this repository's labels for the G3 and acceptance-matrix clauses that apply to the model-free lexical path. Semantic and hybrid retrieval are out of scope here.

states.covered: Every named test exists, runs unconditionally and exercises the clause. evidence lists the tests and covers states what they show.
states.pending: No test shows the clause. evidence is empty and pending_reason says what is missing. partial_evidence lists adjacent tests that do not satisfy it.

clauses.clause: Erased or purged evidence is not found by a later search.
clauses.pending_reason: The application catalogue has no operation that erases or purges evidence, documents or records, so there is no erase-then-search path to run. Tombstoned evidence is excluded (LEX-02) but a tombstone is not an erase.

clauses.clause: Tombstoned evidence is excluded from the search frontier unless the request asks for it, and asking never widens the permission filter.
clauses.covers: Default exclusion, the opt-in, the ACL filter surviving the opt-in, and a later unrelated event not un-tombstoning an artifact.

clauses.clause: A workspace backed up and restored returns the same ranked results.
clauses.covers: A workspace with a built search projection is backed up with the production online-backup path, verified, restored into a fresh directory with the source deleted, and reopened as the service starts. The restored run is current (the start-up build activates nothing) with the same run id, build digest, checkpoint and document count, the artifact checksums are unchanged, and evidence.search returns byte-identical pages, including a relevance order, a recency tie-break, an empty result and a paged result, for six queries.

clauses.clause: A workspace migrated only to schema 0012 builds the search projection and answers a ranked search.
clauses.covers: The migrator stopped at 0012 reports user_version 12, and the build and the ranking over that workspace equal the head-schema ranking; the migration's table shape and idempotence.

clauses.clause: BM25 scoring uses statistics from the authorised frontier only, and new evidence starts a fresh projection run.
clauses.covers: Through evidence.search, evidence is added (a stale-projection refusal until a fresh run is built), tombstoned, un-tombstoned, restricted and released, and the order of the same matching items follows the average length of the authorised frontier at each step: unmatched filler lifts it and reverses the order, removing the filler reverses it back, and a 340-occurrence restricted item moves nothing until its label is withdrawn. The rare-term matrix shows document frequency in the match set as holders of a rare term come and go, restricted holders never counted. BM25's idf is one constant per single-phrase query, so it cannot reorder a result and is not claimed here.

clauses.clause: A search in one workspace cannot return another workspace's evidence, and no cache is shared between workspaces.
clauses.covers: Two migrated workspaces open in one process with the same evidence ids, native ids, checksums, checkpoint and projection run id. Interleaved and repeated searches return each workspace's own evidence, count and rank; the other workspace's request is refused by the binding; each connection's session projection holds only its own documents; new evidence in one workspace leaves the other level and unchanged; and a continuation token minted in one workspace is refused in the other even though both rankings have the same snapshot, so the process-wide token store is isolated by workspace.

clauses.clause: A captured source is found by evidence.search, ranks first, and the Context Pack built for the same query cites the record and its section.
clauses.covers: The installed journey seeds one captured source and one approved record. The journey fails unless evidence.search and knowledge.search return them first and context_pack.build cites the record and a governed_record section, identically on a second build. With one candidate this proves position and citation, not discrimination between competing candidates (LEX-05 and the ranking tests do that). The journey runs in package qualification, not under pytest.
